paragraphs: Children in care across the West Midlands are looked after by the region's councils, each of which runs its own fostering service, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. Figures reported in April 2021 put the number of looked-after children in the West Midlands at 10,700 in 2020, up from 10,060 in 2018, with the number living in residential care rising from 1,230 to 1,450 over the same period.

That growth led Staffordshire County Council and Dudley Council to set up the Big Fostering Partnership in 2021, a pilot backed by the government's Life Chances Fund and social investors. Its aim was to find long-term, nurturing foster homes for children aged seven to sixteen who were then living in children's homes, many of whom had been through trauma, so that more of them could grow up in a family.

Councils in the region also recruit for themselves. Solihull's Foster for Solihull campaign, for example, welcomes applicants from all walks of life, with or without children of their own, single people and those in work, and says its carers can live anywhere in the West Midlands, not only in Solihull. It promises round-the-clock access to an experienced fostering team, local training and a community of other carers.

Because the West Midlands covers so many councils, the best first step is to look at the page for your own town or borough as well as this one. Speak to your council and to two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about the ages of children they most need homes for, the training and out-of-hours support on offer, and what they pay, before you decide.
